title: observability: token-level cost/latency + KV tracing dashboard enhancements and alert tuning
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Improve token-level observability for production inference to make cost/latency regressions and KV-cache behavior easier to diagnose. This PR adds new token-level metrics, enriches tracing spans with KV cache metadata, updates the Token Cost/Latency dashboard, and applies alert tuning based on recent incident postmortem (ENG-5678).

Summary of changes: - Add token-level metrics collector (token_cost_ms, token_cost_usd, token_latency_ms, token_cache_hit, token_cache_miss) with per-model and per-route labels. - Enrich inference tracing spans with kv.cache_hit, kv.cache_read_bytes, kv.lookup_latency_ms to enable end-to-end correlation in distributed traces. - Dashboard: update Token Cost & Latency dashboard tiles to show per-route percentile latencies, token-level cost breakdown, KV hit-rate heatmap, and top-N regression examples. - Alerts: tune SLO alerts and add new aggregation alert for token-level P99 latency on high-throughput routes; add an anomalous-cost spike alert (90th percentile daily increase > 3x) that runs on token_cost_usd metric. - Docs: add an observability runbook section describing how to interpret the new tiles and recommended remediation steps. - Backfill: add a small migration to backfill KV cache hit-rate for the last 7 days where available (best-effort).

Testing: Unit tests added for the metrics collector and trace enrichment. Integration tests run in CI against a local telemetry stack (Prometheus + Jaeger). Dashboard snapshots were validated in staging with synthetic workloads reproducing cache hit/miss scenarios. Alert rules were dogfooded for 48 hours in canary before rolling to prod.

Rollout plan: feature-flag the trace enrichment (telemetry.kv_enrichment) and rollout in three phases: staging -> canary -> global. Dashboard changes are non-breaking; alerts are disabled by default and enabled after a monitoring window.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps metric names stable and uses label cardinality guards (route/model) to avoid unbounded label explosion. See linked Linear tasks for follow-ups (OBS-1023).
commits: feat(tracing): enrich inference spans with kv cache metadata
chore(dashboards): update token cost/latency dashboard tiles and queries
chore(alerts): new token-level p99 latency and anomalous-cost spike rules
docs(observability): add runbook and dashboard guide
test(telemetry): integration tests for metrics + traces
migrations: backfill kv cache hit-rate for last 7 days
fix(ci): address flaky telemetry e2e (retry on Jaeger startup)
review_thread: Jordan Lee (reviewer): API looks good — can you add a short note about label cardinality limits?
Ava Chen (author): Added comment in token_metrics_collector.go and added unit tests to assert cardinality guard behavior.
Samir Patel (reviewer): Alert thresholds LGTM but suggest lowering sensitivity for low-volume routes. Recommend aggregated alert for routes with >500 reqs/min.
Ava Chen (author): Implemented aggregation condition and added documentation on which routes to include in SLO on rollout.
Maya Gupta (reviewer): Tracing enrichment looks safe but please ensure PII is not added to spans.
Ava Chen (author): Confirmed: only kv cache metadata (hit/miss, lookup latency, bytes) added; redaction tests added.
Lucas Brown (approver): Verified dashboard snapshots in staging and canary + CI green. Approving for merge.
release_notes:
- Added token-level cost and latency metrics (per-model, per-route)
- Enriched traces with KV cache metadata to help correlate cache behavior with latency/cost
- Updated Token Cost & Latency dashboard with KV heatmaps and regression examples
- New alerts: token-level P99 latency aggregation and anomalous-cost spike detection
- Observability runbook and guidance added
